headline: Record fee earnings and AUM offset a lower GAAP profit y/y
summary_short: Carlyle's Q2 2026 revenue was $1,123.5M and GAAP net income attributable to common stockholders was $137.1M ($0.38/share basic) — down 57.1% y/y but a rebound from Q1's loss — while non-GAAP Fee Related Earnings hit a record $358M and Distributable Earnings per share rose to $1.07.
summary_long: GAAP income before taxes was $273.8M (24.4% margin), rebounding from a $179M pretax loss in Q1 2026 but down 37.9% y/y as total revenue fell 28.6% y/y to $1,123.5M on lower investment income including performance allocations ($113.9M vs $694.0M in Q2 2025). Away from GAAP, Fee Related Earnings hit a record $358M (+10.8% y/y, 47% margin) and Distributable Earnings rose 9.6% y/y to $472.3M pretax, or $1.07/share after tax (+17.6% y/y). Total AUM reached a record $485B (+4% y/y); fee-earning AUM was $334B (+3% y/y). Carlyle declared a $0.35/share dividend and repurchased or withheld 6.7M shares for $304M, with $1.6B of repurchase capacity remaining. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Investment income including performance allocations fell to $113.9M from $694.0M in Q2 2025, reflecting unrealized allocations in Global Credit and AlpInvest strategies, partly offset by a reversal in the seventh U.S. Buyout fund.

Rebounded to a $273.8M profit from a $179M loss in Q1 2026 (derived from YTD-minus-Q2 arithmetic on the primary table); still down y/y as investment income including performance allocations was much lower than Q2 2025.
Rose to $358M from $323M in Q2 2025 (+11% per the release), driven by higher capital-markets and transaction fees in Global Private Equity, partly offset by a $13M drop in catch-up management fees.

Segment fee revenues rose to $759.3M from $676.2M a year ago on higher transaction/portfolio-advisory and fee-related performance revenues, outpacing higher segment expenses; the release gives no further qualitative cause.
Grew 2% q/q and 4% y/y on a 16% increase in Carlyle AlpInvest AUM and a 4% increase in Global Credit AUM, partly offset by a 1% decline in Global Private Equity AUM.
Held at $0.35/share, unchanged from Q1 2026 and Q2 2025; Carlyle separately disclosed $304M of share repurchases/withholding in the quarter with $1.6B remaining under its $2.0B authorization.
